statement: If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the squares on the unequal segments of the whole are double of the square on the half and of the square on the straight line between the points of section.
heath_proof: For let a straight line AB be cut into equal segments at C, and into unequal segments at D; I say that the squares on AD, DB are double of the squares on AC, CD. For let CE be drawn from C at right angles to AB, and let it be made equal to either AC or CB; let EA, EB be joined, let DF be drawn through D parallel to EC, and FG through F parallel to AB, and let AF be joined. Then, since AC is equal to CE, the angle EAC is also equal to the angle AEC. And, since the angle at C is right, the remaining angles EAC, AEC are equal to one right angle. [I. 32] And they are equal; therefore each of the angles CEA, CAE is half a right angle. For the same reason each of the angles CEB, EBC is also half a right angle; therefore the whole angle AEB is right. And, since the angle GEF is half a right angle, and the angle EGF is right, for it is equal to the interior and opposite angle ECB, [I. 29] the remaining angle EFG is half a right angle; [I. 32] therefore the angle GEF is equal to the angle EFG, so that the side EG is also equal to GF. [I. 6] Again, since the angle at B is half a right angle, and the angle FDB is right, for it is again equal to the interior and opposite angle ECB, [I. 29] the remaining angle BFD is half a right angle; [I. 32]therefore the angle at B is equal to the angle DFB, so that the side FD is also equal to the side DB. [I. 6]  Now, since AC is equal to CE, the square on AC is also equal to the square on CE; therefore the squares on AC, CE are double of the square on AC. But the square on EA is equal to the squares on AC, CE, for the angle ACE is right; [I. 47] therefore the square on EA is double of the square on AC. Again, since EG is equal to GF, the square on EG is also equal to the square on GF; therefore the squares on EG, GF are double of the square on GF. But the square on EF is equal to the squares on EG, GF; therefore the square on EF is double of the square on GF. But GF is equal to CD; [I. 34] therefore the square on EF is double of the square on CD. But the square on EA is also double of the square on AC; therefore the squares on AE, EF are double of the squares on AC, CD. And the square on AF is equal to the squares on AE, EF, for the angle AEF is right; [I. 47] therefore the square on AF is double of the squares on AC, CD. But the squares on AD, DF are equal to the square on AF, for the angle at D is right; [I. 47] therefore the squares on AD, DF are double of the squares on AC, CD. And DF is equal to DB; therefore the squares on AD, DB are double of the squares on AC, CD.

**Statement:** If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the squares on the unequal segments of the whole are double of the square on the half and of the square on the straight line between the points of section.

**Step 1.** Let the straight line AB be cut into equal segments at C and into unequal segments at D, so that AC = CB, and let D lie between C and B. It is to be proved that the squares on AD, DB together are double of the squares on AC, CD together.

**Step 2.** From C draw CE at right angles to AB (1.11); produce it as far as needed (P2) and cut off CE equal to AC (1.3), so that CE is also equal to CB (CN1). Join EA and EB (P1).

**Step 3.** Through D draw DF parallel to CE (1.31), meeting EB at F; through F draw FG parallel to AB (1.31), meeting CE at G. Join AF (P1).

**Step 4.** Since CA = CE, the angle EAC is equal to the angle AEC (1.5). Since CE stands at right angles to AB, the angles ACE and ECB are right (D1.10). In the triangle ACE the three angles are together equal to two right angles (1.32); the angle ACE being right, the remaining angles AEC, EAC are together equal to one right angle (CN3). Being equal to one another, each of them is half a right angle.

**Step 5.** In the same way, since CB = CE, in the triangle ECB the angles CEB, EBC are equal (1.5), and together they are equal to one right angle (1.32, CN3); so each of them is half a right angle.

**Step 6.** Therefore the whole angle AEB, made up of the angles AEC and CEB, each half a right angle, is a right angle.

**Step 7.** Since GF is parallel to CB and the straight line EC falls upon them, the exterior angle EGF is equal to the interior and opposite angle ECB (1.29), which is right; so the angle EGF is right. The angle GEF is the same as the angle CEB, which is half a right angle (Step 5). Hence in the triangle EGF the remaining angle EFG is half a right angle (1.32, CN3), so that the angle GEF is equal to the angle EFG, and therefore the side GE is equal to the side GF (1.6).

**Step 8.** Since DF is parallel to CE and the straight line AB falls upon them, the exterior angle FDB is equal to the interior and opposite angle ECD (1.29), which is right; so the angle FDB is right. The angle DBF is the same as the angle EBC, which is half a right angle (Step 5). Hence in the triangle DFB the remaining angle DFB is half a right angle (1.32, CN3), so that the angle DFB is equal to the angle DBF, and therefore the side DF is equal to the side DB (1.6).

**Step 9.** Since AC = CE, the square on AC is equal to the square on CE; hence the squares on AC, CE together are double of the square on AC. But the angle ACE is right, so the square on EA is equal to the squares on AC, CE (1.47). Therefore the square on EA is double of the square on AC (CN1).

**Step 10.** Since EG = GF (Step 7), the square on EG is equal to the square on GF; hence the squares on EG, GF together are double of the square on GF. But the angle EGF is right (Step 7), so the square on EF is equal to the squares on EG, GF (1.47). Therefore the square on EF is double of the square on GF (CN1). Now CG is parallel to DF and GF is parallel to CD, so CDFG is a parallelogram, and its opposite sides GF, CD are equal (1.34). Therefore the square on EF is double of the square on CD.

**Step 11.** Adding these results, the squares on AE, EF together are double of the squares on AC, CD together (CN2).

**Step 12.** But the angle AEF is right (Step 6), so the square on AF is equal to the squares on AE, EF (1.47). Therefore the square on AF is double of the squares on AC, CD together (CN1).

**Step 13.** Since the angle FDB is right (Step 8), and the adjacent angles ADF, FDB are together equal to two right angles (1.13), the angle ADF is also right (CN3). Therefore the square on AF is equal to the squares on AD, DF (1.47).

**Step 14.** And DF = DB (Step 8), so the square on DF is equal to the square on DB; hence the squares on AD, DF together are equal to the squares on AD, DB together (CN2), and so the squares on AD, DB together are equal to the square on AF (CN1). Therefore the squares on AD, DB together are double of the squares on AC, CD together (CN1).

**Step 15.** Therefore, if a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the squares on the unequal segments of the whole are double of the square on the half and of the square on the straight line between the points of section. Q.E.D.
